$comment: Sizes are world pixels (320 x 180 view). Painted files are 4x. See content/README.md. Every carving is listed one world pixel wider and taller than its figure, for the one-pixel shadow it throws down and to the left; the game blits it one pixel left of the figure's place. A carving with two frames has frame 0 facing right and frame 1 facing left, each lit from the upper right; one with one frame is painted the way it stands. Drawn by the game and not listed: the sky and the sun; the Marvdasht plain and its far hills; the treads, risers and side masonry of every stair, drawn by the code that draws the ashlar tiles so the two are one masonry; the Gate's piers (their blocks, broken tops and plinths); the columns of the Gate and of the Apadana, one drawing (fluted shaft, square double plinth or bell base, broken top, no capital); the polished benches; the Tachara's door jambs and the cavetto cornices on its lintels; the Apadana façade's wall, merlons, registers, mouldings, the flights' slopes, the plain band and the blank; the shelter and its posts; the dark edge each guard has standing out in the court; the tourist turned to stone (the 'carved' death), drawn in front of the guards where he died, which the game makes from his own frame; the visitors' names (the game's own nameScratch). The exit is the game's own plain exit.

assets.what: The Marvdasht plain's earth, dry and dusty, under the plain and under the foot of the stair.
The same with sky over it: the plain's trodden surface where he walks in.
The terrace's masonry: big grey limestone blocks, unmortared, in courses, an empty dovetail clamp socket at some joints. Everything under a floor, under every stair and under the landing.
The same with sky over it: the bare top of a course, on the landing. Under a stair the game uses the plain tile, because the stair is over it.
The terrace's top course with something on it. Not used in the level as built; listed because the code can ask for it.
The terrace's surface, dusty grey-buff over the top course: the Gate, the Tachara's platform and the Apadana's court.
A bull of the west portal of the Gate of All Nations, in profile, four legs, on the passage wall. Faces left, out of the gate, as it stands; not flipped.
A human-headed winged bull of the east portal, in profile: tall cylindrical crown, curled beard, wing swept back, four legs. Faces right, out of the gate, as it stands; not flipped.
A lintel of the Tachara in its dark polished limestone, with something on top of it. Not used in the level as built; listed because the code can ask for it.
A lintel of the Tachara, one tile, dark polished limestone with a soft highlight, sky over it. Solid: he bumps his head on it in the doorway.

A window or niche block of the Tachara standing alone, one stone of the dark polished limestone, a stepped frame round a dark opening, a cavetto cornice on top. Windows and niches are the same from outside: one painting for both.

The carving on the far jamb of a Tachara doorway: the king walking out of the hall, an attendant behind him, drawn smaller, holding the parasol over him. In the polished stone. Two frames: walking right, walking left.

A guard of the east stair's central projection: fluted hat, curled beard, long robe, spear upright in front of him. All eight are this one figure, in the wall and standing out in the court. Two frames: facing right (the left file), facing left (the right file).
A sphinx seated under the winged disc, a lion's body, a crowned and bearded man's head, a wing curving up, facing the disc. Two frames: facing right, facing left.
The winged disc at the head of the central projection: small and plain, a disc, two wings, a tail. Never animated.
The lion leaping on the bull, in the angle under each flight by the central projection. Two frames: as on the left flight, and mirrored for the right.
A delegate of the south wing walking right with his gift. Every delegate in the three registers is this one figure. Faces right as it stands.
The usher at the head of each delegation, walking right and holding the leader's hand behind him. Faces right as it stands.
A Persian noble of the north wing, fluted hat and long robe, walking left. Faces left as it stands; not flipped.
A Median noble of the north wing, rounded cap, belted tunic and trousers, walking left. Faces left as it stands; not flipped.
A cypress, carved between the delegations of the south wing and in a row up each flight.
